clue.text: Hamlet's uncle was one

parts.note: Claudius murdered his brother, the reigning King of Denmark, to take his throne and his queen

explanation.surface: A literary quiz question about Shakespeare's villain Claudius.
explanation.definitionFit: Killing a monarch is the crime of king-murder, and someone who commits it bears the same name.

clue.text: A check on the presents ?

parts.note: presents read as people who are present, not gifts: a check on attendance

explanation.surface: Inspecting the gifts under the Christmas tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading out names to record who is in attendance checks which people are there.

clue.text: Minister who was happy to put on weight?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece put on another sits above it

parts.note: glad means happy
a stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A politician who was content to gain weight.
explanation.walkthrough: William Gladstone was a Victorian prime minister; a stone (14 lb) is the British unit for body weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladstone served four times as prime minister, the chief government minister.

clue.text: To study this island is hard

definitions.text: To study this island is hard

parts.words: To study this island is hard
parts.note: study gives CON; adding the island's name after it makes a word meaning hard, like set cement

explanation.surface: A complaint that learning about this island is difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: This works backwards: CON (to study) followed by the island gives a building material that is hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean island south of Greece is the place meant.

clue.text: A disc to reform some robbers

indicators.note: to reform something is to form it again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reshaping a disc to make robbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of armed gangs of bandits in India and Burma are robbers.

clue.text: Architectural feature one could count on

definitions.meaning: the flat slab forming the top of a column's capital
a frame of beads slid along wires for doing sums

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the slab crowning a classical column and the bead-frame calculator used for arithmetic.

clue.text: Formidable female made cuts in fighting services ?

definitions.meaning: a weapon for hacking in combat

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a fierce domineering woman and the broad-bladed weapon used for chopping in warfare.

clue.text: They need a crew to get them out

definitions.text: They need a crew to get them out

parts.words: They need a crew to get them out
parts.note: add crew after them and they make the tool that pulls them from bottles

explanation.surface: A boat or ship that needs sailors to take it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle stoppers are removed with a spiral tool whose name is them plus screw.

clue.text: This is seen long before sunset

definitions.text: This is seen long before sunset

parts.words: This is seen long before sunset
parts.note: long read as lengthened: in late afternoon, the dark shape cast by an object stretches out

explanation.surface: Something visible well ahead of evening.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark area cast by a body blocking sunlight grows long as the sun sinks.

clue.text: Compensation for loss of sound and vision?

definitions.meaning: something that balances out a loss

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a counterbalancing amount, and split in two, a TV set switched off gives no sound or picture.

clue.text: It's quite a departure from work

definitions.text: It's quite a departure from work

parts.words: It's quite a departure from work
parts.note: a departure from work is time off granted by an employer, a holiday or furlough

explanation.surface: A remark that something is very different from one's usual job.
explanation.definitionFit: Permission for absence from duty, as in annual or sick holiday, is this kind of departure.

clue.text: No waiting here!

parts.note: a parking-sign phrase reread as an eating place without table service, where diners fetch their own food

explanation.surface: A no-parking sign by the roadside.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-service eating place has no table service, so nobody waits on the customers.

clue.text: Examples of beauty being only skin deep?

definitions.text: Examples of beauty being only skin deep?

parts.words: Examples of beauty being only skin deep?
parts.note: the proverb about superficial looks reread literally: products of beauty applied only to the skin

explanation.surface: A cynical reflection on the proverb that beauty is only skin deep.
explanation.definitionFit: Make-up and creams are beauty products that sit literally on the surface of the skin.

clue.text: Give the girl a ring-one way to catch her

parts.note: a lass is a girl
the letter O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: Courtship advice: phone the girl if you want to win her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give the girl a ring' sounds like telephoning her; it is LASS followed by the ring-shaped O.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope noose thrown by cowboys is a way to catch an animal, here jokingly the girl.

clue.text: Fool has mislaid the scrubbers

indicators.note: letters that have been mislaid are put in the wrong places, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A careless person has lost the scrubbing brushes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried gourd sponges are used for scrubbing the skin in the bath.

clue.text: They are dropped silently

parts.note: the breathed H sounds left unpronounced in a Cockney accent

explanation.surface: Things let fall without a sound.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping one's aitches, saying 'ouse' for 'house', is a British accent marker.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathy H sounds are the consonants dropped in some accents, so they go unspoken.

clue.text: Topping sparklers !

parts.note: topping read as worn on top of the head, sparklers as glittering jewels

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic cry of 'Super fireworks!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' is old British slang for excellent, so the surface praises fireworks.
explanation.definitionFit: Jewelled coronets are worn on the head and glitter with gems.

clue.text: Much meaning in the plot, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: much is a lot, and meaning is meant: a lot meant

explanation.surface: A great deal of significance in the story's storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is a small rented plot of land for growing vegetables in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rented patch of ground for growing vegetables is a garden plot.

clue.text: Chesterton's man named the day

definitions.meaning: G K Chesterton's novel 'The Man Who Was' this day

explanation.definitionFit: Chesterton's spy novel names its hero after a weekday, the one between Wednesday and Friday.

clue.text: Ring for the man in charge

definitions.meaning: a guard ring worn to stop another ring slipping off the finger

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a guard ring holding a wedding band in place and a custodian who looks after something.

clue.text: It's uncommonly distinguished

parts.note: uncommonly read literally: something set apart by being uncommon

explanation.surface: Praise for something exceptionally fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seldom found is marked out by its scarcity.

clue.text: Pope's Ralph Allen did good by this

definitions.text: Pope's Ralph Allen did good by this

parts.words: Pope's Ralph Allen did good by this
parts.note: Alexander Pope wrote of the philanthropist Allen that he would 'do good by' this means, and blush to find it fame

explanation.surface: A literary allusion to Pope's praise of his patron Ralph Allen.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Pope's Epilogue to the Satires: 'Let humble Allen, with an awkward shame, / Do good by ... and blush to find it fame.'
explanation.definitionFit: Secret, unseen action is how Allen did his charity, quietly and without display.

clue.text: Saint converted his twin

indicators.note: converted means changed into a different form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A holy man won his brother over to the faith.
explanation.walkthrough: St Swithin's Day, 15 July, is tied to the British folklore that rain on it means forty more days of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Swithin was a ninth-century Bishop of Winchester venerated as a saint.

clue.text: Composer's lines on a battleship

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the old railway lines
HMS, His or Her Majesty's Ship, prefixes a Royal Navy vessel

explanation.surface: A composer's verses written aboard a warship.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Brahms was a nineteenth-century German composer of symphonies.

clue.text: For instance the sun first seen in flight

definitions.meaning: something that gets up, as the sun comes up each morning
the upright part of a stair step, met first on a flight of stairs

explanation.definitionFit: The word means one who gets up, like the rising sun, and the vertical board of each stair in a staircase.

clue.text: First battle of certain (about 1,000) tanks

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is put around the other

parts.note: certain, as in 'certain people', means some
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Recalling the first battle in which tanks appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: tanks first went into battle on this river in 1916.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanks were first used in combat on the Somme in September 1916.

clue.text: Eavesdrop literally during the fall

parts.note: eavesdrop split literally into eaves and drop: what drips off the eaves while precipitation falls

explanation.surface: Listening in secretly, as autumn arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Water dripping from a roof's eaves during a shower is the precipitation itself.

clue.text: Apart from its head, the mammal is sound

definitions.text: Apart from its head, the mammal is sound

parts.words: Apart from its head, the mammal is sound
parts.note: drop the first letter of the sea mammal and what remains means healthy

explanation.surface: A vet's verdict that the animal is fine except for its head.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest marine mammal loses its W to leave a word for healthy.

clue.text: Borderline needlework

parts.note: borderline read as a line along a border: sewing that finishes the edge of fabric

explanation.surface: Sewing that is only just acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative stitch used to finish the turned-up edge of cloth is done along its border.

clue.text: Get better by noon ?

parts.note: by noon split as the close of the morning, i.e. the end of a.m., while get better means improve

explanation.surface: Hoping to recover from illness before midday.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct or improve something is to make it better; split up, the letters also say morning's close.

clue.text: Jenny's such a fool

parts.note: a jenny is a female donkey, and a donkey is slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark that Jenny is an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jenny' looks like a woman's name; it is the word for a female donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A female donkey is a jenny, and calling someone a donkey means they are silly.

clue.text: What any crest possibly indicates

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A heraldic crest suggests a family's lineage.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a coat of arms points to one's forebears.
explanation.definitionFit: A heraldic crest records lineage, so it indicates a family's line of descent.
